Optional: name, x, y (pixel center), width, height (render bounds), size/depth/aspect/cornerRadius (geometry), color, metalness (0..1), roughness (0..1), materialKind (physical|basic), emissive, mapAssetId (an image asset id to texture onto the phone screen, e.g. a wallpaper from import_image_layer), rotationX/Y/Z (initial degrees), fov, cameraDistance, environment (studio|dark|none — studio gives realistic reflections on metal/glass), groundShadow (true drops a soft contact shadow under the object), startTime, duration. Animate the spin with animate_layer property 'transform.rotation.y' (or .x/.z) — e.g. 0→360 over 4s shows the whole device turning in 3D. ZOOM/DOLLY: keyframe 'transform.position.z' — +1 pushes the camera 2x closer (zoom in), +2 = 4x, negative pulls back. Combine a position.z 0→1.5 ramp with a rotation.y tilt for a cinematic push-in.

name: morph_motion_shape
title: Morph a shape into another shape
description: Animate a shape MORPHING into a different shape (After Effects-style path morph): the outline smoothly transforms, point-by-point, from one form to another. Give the source shape (layerId) and a target — toLayerId (morph into another shape layer's outline), toShapeType (rectangle|circle|ellipse|triangle|polygon|star|arrow|line, built at toWidth×toHeight, defaulting to the source size), or toPath (an explicit SVG path string centered at the origin — supply any custom outline, e.g. a logo or icon). Morph runs fromTime (default 0) → toTime with optional easing. Works between completely different shapes (arc-length resampling). Pair with a 'lift' — animate transform.position.z and transform.scale — to pop a button off a UI surface and then morph it into an icon.

name: set_motion_shape_path
title: Set bezier shape path
description: Replace the whole outline of a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path'). points is an array of >=2 finite {x,y,inX?,inY?,outX?,outY?} vertices in layer-local pixel coordinates, where inX/inY and outX/outY are ABSOLUTE bezier control-handle coordinates (in = handle from the previous point, out = handle toward the next point); omit handles for straight corners. closed (default keeps the layer's current pathClosed) marks the path as a closed loop. The layer must have shapeType:'path' — create one via add_motion_layer with shapeType:'path'.

name: edit_motion_shape_path_point
title: Edit bezier shape path point
description: Edit a single vertex (by index, 0-based) of a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path'). Pass x/y to move the anchor (its handles move with it), and/or inX/inY (incoming handle) / outX/outY (outgoing handle) as ABSOLUTE layer-local pixel coordinates. Supply at least one of x/y/inX/inY/outX/outY. Use insert_motion_shape_path_point / remove_motion_shape_path_point to change the point count.

name: insert_motion_shape_path_point
title: Insert bezier shape path point
description: Insert a vertex into a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path') AFTER the given index (0-based). Pass an explicit point {x,y,inX?,inY?,outX?,outY?} (layer-local pixels, absolute handles) or omit it to insert a midpoint on the segment following afterIndex. Increases the point count by one.

name: remove_motion_shape_path_point
title: Remove bezier shape path point
description: Remove the vertex at index (0-based) from a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path'). Refuses (INVALID_PARAMS) when the path is already at its minimum (2 points for an open path, 3 for a closed one).

name: add_motion_shape_path_keyframe
title: Add bezier shape path keyframe
description: Add or replace a shape.pathData keyframe at a time on a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path') so its outline animates/morphs over time. Supply pathData (an SVG path string) or points (an array of >=2 {x,y,inX?,inY?,outX?,outY?} vertices, layer-local pixels, absolute handles); omit both to snapshot the layer's CURRENT path. easing is any known easing name. Re-calling at the same time replaces that keyframe.

name: transform_motion_keyframes
title: Transform a property's keyframes
description: Batch-transform ALL keyframes of one property on a motion layer (the AE graph-editor keyframe ops). op is: 'reverse' (mirror values across the property's own time span), 'scale' (stretch/compress times about the first keyframe by factor scale>0 — 2 doubles the spacing), or 'duplicate' (copy every keyframe shifted by offset seconds, merging onto existing). scale is required for 'scale'; offset (may be negative) is required for 'duplicate'. property is any animatable id (transform.*, shape style properties like shape.width, shape.fill.opacity, effect.<id>.<param>, mask.<id>.<prop>, modifier.<id>.<prop>, ...) — note shape path data is not an animatable id here; animate a PEN path with add_motion_shape_path_keyframe. Use copy_motion_keyframes / paste_motion_keyframes to move keys between different properties. Any roving keyframes on the property keep constant-speed spacing: their times are re-derived from the surrounding anchors after the op, so reverse/scale/duplicate reposition them automatically.

name: copy_motion_keyframes
title: Copy a property's keyframes
description: Read a motion layer property's keyframes into a portable clipboard payload (relative time offsets, values, and easings) for inspection or for feeding paste_motion_keyframes. Returns data.clipboard plus entryCount, span (seconds), and sourceProperty. NOT_FOUND if the property has no keyframes. The roving flag is not carried in the clipboard — pasted keyframes start non-roving, and on the destination property any existing roving keyframes re-derive their constant-speed times after the merge.

name: paste_motion_keyframes
title: Paste keyframes onto a property
description: Copy every keyframe from fromProperty and paste them onto toProperty of the SAME layer, preserving relative spacing and easing, shifted so the run starts at (fromProperty's first keyframe time + timeOffset seconds, default 0). Existing keyframes on toProperty are kept (pasted keys merge, replacing any at identical times). Both properties must be valid animatable ids. Pasted keyframes are never roving; any roving keyframes already on toProperty re-derive their constant-speed times after the merge. Use transform_motion_keyframes to reverse/scale/duplicate keys in place on a single property.

name: add_motion_3d_scene
title: Create a 3D scene (multi-object + cinematic camera)
description: Create ONE scene3d layer that is a FULL 3D WORLD — many objects sharing a camera, lights, and an optional room — instead of a single object. Declarative: you place objects in 3D and the engine does all the WebGL. This legacy-compatible tool now also creates semantic creation assets/objects plus a motion-scene3d render binding, so the scene remains editable in Motion Creator's Creation workspace. `objects` is an array; each entry: { kind (box|rounded-box|sphere|cylinder|cone|torus|icosahedron|plane|phone|model|text3d|soccer-ball|open-box|room), name, x,y,z (world position), rotationX/Y/Z (deg), scaleX/Y/Z, size, depth, aspect, cornerRadius, modelUrl (for model), text+extrude (for text3d), panelTexts (labels for soccer-ball), lidAngle (open-box, deg), color, metalness, roughness, materialKind, emissive, mapAssetId, opacity, key, objectId, partId, tags }. `camera`: { posX,posY,posZ, targetX,targetY,targetZ, fov, near, far }. `room`: { enabled, size, wallColor, floorColor } (camera flies in from the open +Z front). Optional environment (studio|dark|none), groundShadow. Then keyframe motion with animate_scene_camera + animate_scene_object. Returns layerId + render object ids plus semantic scene/object ids.

name: add_scene_object
title: Add an object to a 3D scene
description: Append one object to an existing scene3d layer (created by add_motion_3d_scene). Same fields as one entry of add_motion_3d_scene's `objects`. When the layer has a semantic creation binding, or can be recovered into one, this also appends an editable creation asset/object and render binding so Motion Creator can inspect and revise it later. Returns the render objectId plus semantic creation ids.

name: set_motion_scene_object
title: Edit an object in a 3D scene
description: Statically edit one object inside a multi-object scene3d layer (created by add_motion_3d_scene). Merge only the fields you pass onto the object matched by objectId. transform: { position?{x,y,z}, rotation?{x,y,z} (deg), scale?{x,y,z} }. material: { color?, metalness?, roughness?, emissive?, emissiveIntensity?, opacity?, transmission? (0..1 glass), ior? (index of refraction), clearcoat? (0..1), clearcoatRoughness? (0..1), materialKind? (physical|basic), mapAssetId?, normalMapAssetId?, roughnessMapAssetId?, metalnessMapAssetId? } (metalness/roughness/opacity/transmission/clearcoat/clearcoatRoughness clamp to 0..1). geometry: { kind?(box|rounded-box|sphere|cylinder|cone|torus|icosahedron|plane|phone|model|text3d|soccer-ball|open-box|room), size?, depth?, cornerRadius?, aspect?, modelUrl? (for kind=model), text? (for kind=text3d), extrude? (text3d extrusion fraction), panelTexts? (string[] for soccer-ball) }. lidAngle? (deg, for kind=open-box) is set at the object level. For animated changes use animate_scene_object instead.

name: remove_motion_scene_object
title: Remove an object from a 3D scene
description: Remove one object from a multi-object scene3d layer by objectId. Refuses to remove the last remaining object — delete the scene3d layer instead when you want an empty scene.

name: set_motion_scene_camera
title: Set the static 3D scene camera
description: Set the static (non-animated) cinematic camera on a scene3d layer. position?{x,y,z}, target?{x,y,z}, fov? (degrees), near? (near clip plane distance), far? (far clip plane distance). Only the fields you pass change. Complements animate_scene_camera, which keyframes the camera over time.

name: animate_scene_camera
title: Animate the 3D scene camera
description: Keyframe the cinematic camera of a scene3d layer — the 'camera at this angle at this time, move this way, orbit this point' control. `position` and `target` are arrays of { time, x, y, z, easing }; `fov` is an array of { time, value, easing }. Times in seconds. Re-calling replaces the camera keyframes. When the layer is bound to an editable creation scene, this also mirrors the camera animation into creation animation state for recovery and later editing. Example fly-in then orbit: position [{time:0,x:0,y:4,z:24},{time:1.4,x:0,y:2,z:9},{time:2.4,x:7,y:2,z:7},{time:6,x:-7,y:2,z:7}], target locked on the subject.

name: set_model_animation
title: Set GLB model animation playback
description: Bind a GLB/glTF animation clip to a model inside a scene3d layer so Motion Creator renders the rigged model over time instead of as a static pose. Use clipName or clipIndex to choose a clip; omit both to use the first clip. timeOffset shifts the clip start, playbackRate changes speed, and animationLoop=false clamps on the final frame. For multi-object scenes pass objectId; for a legacy single-model scene3d layer omit objectId.

name: animate_scene_object
title: Animate an object in a 3D scene
description: Keyframe one object inside a scene3d layer in TRUE 3D over time — shake, spin, lift, open. `position`, `rotation` (degrees), `scale` are arrays of { time, x, y, z, easing }; `opacity` and `lidAngle` (open-box) are arrays of { time, value, easing }. Times in seconds. Re-calling replaces that object's keyframes for the channels you pass. When the layer is bound to an editable creation scene, this also mirrors position/rotation/scale/opacity tracks into creation animation state for recovery and later editing. Example lift: position [{time:1.4,x:0,y:0,z:0},{time:2.4,x:0,y:5,z:0}] + rotation spin [{time:1.4,x:0,y:0,z:0},{time:6,x:0,y:720,z:0}].

name: animate_motion_layers
title: Animate motion layers (batch)
description: Apply an animation preset to MANY layers at once with a per-layer stagger — e.g. 'stagger all the cards in with a slide-up'. presetId is one of fade-in, fade-out, slide-up-in, slide-left-in, scale-pop, rotate-in, pulse, float-loop, stroke-draw-on, stroke-pop, gradient-sweep, corner-bloom (see get_capabilities motion.animationPresets). Optional: startTime, duration, stagger (seconds added per layer in layerIds order), distance, intensity. Layers that don't support a shape-only preset are skipped.

name: execute_action
title: Execute action
description: Escape hatch: dispatch any underlying editor action by type + params. Use get_capabilities and the action catalog for valid types.

name: batch_actions
title: Batch actions
description: Dispatch a sequence of raw actions in order; stops on first failure.

name: export_motion_video
title: Export motion video
description: Render a motion composition to a finished video file and return the filename plus width/height/duration/framesRendered and the format actually encoded. format: 'mp4' (H.264, opaque), 'webm-alpha' (VP9 with transparency), or 'mov-prores4444' (ProRes 4444 with transparency); default 'mp4'. On the web build only the desktop app can produce transparent WebM or ProRes — for those formats on web the export normalizes to opaque H.264, so you MUST pass acknowledgeH264Fallback:true to consent (otherwise the export fails with a warning telling you to acknowledge or use desktop). Optional filename overrides the auto-generated name. Inspect data.normalizedToH264 / data.encodedFormat to see what was really written. Expensive — requires confirmation.

name: queue_motion_render
title: Queue motion render
description: Add a motion composition to the render queue for later batch export. format: 'mp4' | 'webm-alpha' | 'mov-prores4444' | 'png-sequence' (default 'mp4'). Optional rangeStart/rangeEnd (seconds, within the composition duration, start<end) render only that span; resolutionScale (1 | 0.5 | 0.25) downscales the output; optional filename overrides the auto name. On the web build transparent WebM and ProRes normalize to opaque H.264 — for those you MUST pass acknowledgeH264Fallback:true to consent (png-sequence is transparent but ZIP-encoded and never needs acknowledgement). Returns data.itemId. Use run_motion_render_queue to render.

name: run_motion_render_queue
title: Run motion render queue
description: Render every queued (or previously failed) item in the motion render queue sequentially and return per-item outcomes (data.outcomes: itemId, status, encodedFormat, filename, error). Items whose cancel was requested are skipped as 'canceled'. Expensive — requires confirmation.

name: list_motion_render_queue
title: List motion render queue
description: List the current motion render queue items (data.items with itemId, compositionId, format, status, progress, and any range/resolutionScale/filename/error).

name: cancel_motion_render_item
title: Cancel motion render item
description: Cancel a queued or in-progress motion render queue item by itemId. A queued item is canceled immediately; a rendering item stops at the next frame boundary. Returns whether the item was found.

name: export_video
title: Export video
description: Render the whole project to a video file (format: mp4|webm|mov, default mp4), upload it to cloud storage, and return a presigned download URL (data.url, valid ~15 min) plus mediaKey/bytes. Expensive — requires confirmation.

name: export_audio
title: Export audio
description: Render the project audio to a file (format: mp3|wav|aac|flac|ogg, default wav), upload it to cloud storage, and return a presigned download URL (data.url, valid ~15 min). Expensive — requires confirmation.

name: transcribe_clip
title: Transcribe clip
description: Transcribe a clip's audio to text/subtitles via the AI service. Expensive — requires confirmation.
